findings.where: artifacts/studio/src/wallet/ActivityMineLedger.tsx (rows composition, ~lines 157-166 and the rows.length===0 empty state)
findings.claim: The Mine ledger collapses rows:null (readback contract: 'null = the record model is unavailable — honest gap, never guessed') into an empty array via `purchases.rows ?? []` and `introductions.rows ?? []`, turning UNAVAILABLE into proven ABSENCE.
findings.evidence: OwnPurchasesReadback/OwnIntroductionsReadback document rows:null as model-unavailable; every sibling surface renders a distinct unavailable branch (ReceiptsBinderPanel.tsx:330, MemberNotificationsBell.tsx:171, ReferralCommissionsPanel.tsx:565, ReferralIntroductionsPanel.tsx:33). Failure path: signed-in S4 member, own-purchase model dark (rows:null with failureReason) → purchases silently missing with no gap notice; if the standing receipt also misses, a seated member is shown 'No on-chain acts on this account yet' + a 'Take your seat' door — a proof-of-absence claim over an unread model, against the page's own 'never a silent gap, never proof of absence' doctrine. Client-only fix; does not block the batch.

findings.claim: The vanity gate has no upper bound: a seat beyond 1,000,000 (Chapter V is open-ended, gate only requires n>=1 + chapter + receipt) would print a negative seniority.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED: n=1000001 → seniorityPct '-0.0001' → 'Seated before -0.0001% of the story — the 1,000,001st of 1,000,000 seats'. Theoretical today (14 seats; 1M is the story's final rung) but the gate carries no n <= STORY_FINAL_SEAT clause.

findings.claim: The collectible's WRITTEN ON-CHAIN line mixes two authorities in one sentence: the DAY comes from the oldest own indexed purchase (own-purchase read-model) while BLOCK + VERIFY come from the continuity spine's entry receipt (lookupMemberReceipt) — the day can belong to a different transaction than the block/anchor beside it if the purchase index misses the entry event.
findings.evidence: member-standing receipt = spine entryTransaction/entryBlock (auth/memberRoster.ts); entryDay = rows[rows.length-1].isoDayUtc from /api/auth/member-purchases (server sorts newest-first, ownPurchaseReadmodel.ts:286-293 — the oldest-index claim itself is CORRECT). Same tx when both models are complete; a one-authority-figure-rule tension only under index incompleteness. Degrades honestly (day omitted) only when rows are null/empty.

findings.claim: The seat-entry row's date column renders the literal lowercase word 'block' instead of the block number, although standing.receipt.block (number|null) is available at composition time.
findings.evidence: LedgerRow.day is null for the seat row ('the block is its coordinate' per the comment) but the coordinate itself is never printed — a founder-visible oddity in the Mine table's first column.

findings.claim: The spine read is a whole-table select with no chainId or numbering-authority scope, resolved by first-match find on entryWallet only.
findings.evidence: Safe today: single-chain deployment, entryWallet unique per doctrine (one identity-bearing entry per member, PK chainId+memberNumber), checksum handled by lowercasing both sides, fail-closed on every branch, DB-gated + 10-min TTL. Noted because the sibling reader (memberRoster.lookupGenesisMember) scopes by authority; a second chain's rows in the table would make find() nondeterministic.
